questions.q: What did Yahweh say those who pursue righteousness should look to?
questions.a: Yahweh said to look at the rock from which you were hewn and to the pit from which you were dug.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do to Abraham?
questions.a: Yahweh called him, blessed him and made him many.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh will comfort Zion, make her wilderness like Eden, and fill her with joy, gladness, thanksgiving, and singing.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would go out from him for the peoples?
questions.a: Yahweh said his law would go out from him, and he would make his justice a light for the peoples.

questions.q: What will Yahweh’s arms do for the peoples?
questions.a: Yahweh’s arms will judge the peoples.

questions.q: What will happen to the heavens, the earth and its inhabitants?
questions.a: The heavens will vanish away like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die.

questions.q: What will continue forever and never fail?
questions.a: Yahweh’s salvation will continue forever, and his righteousness will never fail.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh tell not to be afraid of being insulted by others?
questions.a: Yahweh tells this to those who know what is right and who have his law in their hearts.

questions.q: How long will Yahweh’s righteousness and salvation continue?
questions.a: Yahweh’s righteousness will continue forever, and his salvation will continue to every generation.

questions.q: Who crushed the sea monster, dried up the sea and made the depths of the sea into a way for the redeemed to pass through?
questions.a: The arm of Yahweh did these things.

questions.q: What will overtake and what will flee away from the ransomed of Yahweh when they return and come to Zion?
questions.a: Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh say comforts his people?
questions.a: Yahweh says that he is the one who comforts his people.

questions.q: Who created the heavens and the earth?
questions.a: Yahweh, the maker of his people, created the heavens and the earth.

questions.q: What will soon happen to the prisoner who is bent down?
questions.a: He will soon be set free; he will not die in the pit, and he will not lack bread.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do when the sea’s waves roar?
questions.a: Yahweh makes the sea rest when its waves roar.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say to Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh said to Zion, ‘You are my people.’

questions.q: What did Jerusalem drink from the hand of Yahweh?
questions.a: They drank the cup of Yahweh’s anger; they drank the bowl, the cup of staggering.

questions.q: Who among all the sons of Jerusalem guides her?
questions.a: No one among all the sons she bore guides her, and no one holds her hand.

questions.q: What two things have happened to Jerusalem?
questions.a: Destruction and ruin, and famine and the sword have happened to Jerusalem.

questions.q: Where do Jerusalem’s sons lie?
questions.a: They lie at the head of every street, like an antelope caught in a net.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh tell to listen to him?
questions.a: Yahweh tells the poor, who are staggering but not from wine, to listen to him.

questions.q: What has Yahweh taken from Jerusalem’s hand?
questions.a: Yahweh has taken the cup of staggering, the cup of his anger, from Jerusalem’s hand.

questions.q: After Yahweh takes away the cup of staggering from Jerusalem, who will he give it to?
questions.a: He will put it into the hand of Jerusalem’s tormentors.

commentary.text: Exhortations to trust the Messiah. (Is. 51:1-3) The power of God, and the weakness of man. (Is. 51:4-8) Christ defends his people. (Is. 51:9-16) Their afflictions and deliverances. (Is. 51:17-23)

Is. 51:1-3 It is good for those privileged by the new birth, to consider that they were shapen in sin. This should cause low thoughts of ourselves, and high thoughts of Divine grace. It is the greatest comfort to be made serviceable to the glory of God. The more holiness men have, and the more good they do, the more gladness they have. Let us seriously reflect upon our guilt. To do so will tend to keep the heart humble, and the conscience awake and tender. They make Christ more precious to the soul, and give strength to our attempts and prayers for others.

Is. 51:4-8 The gospel of Christ shall be preached and published. How shall we escape if we neglect it? There is no salvation without righteousness. The soul shall, as to this world, vanish like smoke, and the body be thrown by like a worn-out garment. But those whose happiness is in Christ's righteousness and salvation, will have the comfort of it when time and days shall be no more. Clouds darken the sun, but do not stop its course. The believer will enjoy his portion, while revilers of Christ are in darkness

Is. 51:9-16 The people whom Christ has redeemed with his blood, as well as by his power, will obtain joyful deliverance from every enemy. He that designs such joy for us at last, will he not work such deliverance in the mean time, as our cases require? In this world of changes, it is a short step from joy to sorrow, but in that world, sorrow shall never come in view. They prayed for the display of God's power; he answers them with consolations of his grace. Did we dread to sin against God, we should not fear the frowns of men. Happy is the man that fears God always. And Christ's church shall enjoy security by the power and providence of the Almighty.

Is. 51:17-23 God calls upon his people to mind the things that belong to their everlasting peace. Jerusalem had provoked God, and was made to taste the bitter fruits. Those who should have been her comforters, were their own tormentors. They have no patience by which to keep possesion of their own souls, nor any confidence in God's promise, by which to keep possession of its comfort. Thou art drunken, not as formerly, with the intoxicating cup of Babylon's idolatries, but with the cup of affliction. Know, then, the cause of God's people may for a time seem as lost, but God will protect it, by convincing the conscience, or confounding the projects, of those that strive against it. The oppressors required souls to be subjected to them, that every man should believe and worship as they would have them. But all they could gain by violence was, that people were brought to outward hypocritical conformity, for consciences cannot be forced.
